mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day period when FEDFUNDS was unchanged, p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, the correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline is <0.3, or 60-day returns are not statistically higher than a baseline of neutral labor conditions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above industrial production (INDPRO) suggests strong demand growth that outpaces supply, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive in the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows by at least 2% while INDPRO remains flat over the next week
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) when demand outperformance is present.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 3% in a month indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which typically precedes a sharp drop in equity valuations and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 3% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day window of stable production (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit negative 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when inflation crosses the 2% threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual we use HOUST) coinciding with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) creates a labor market tightening that can drive positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while UNRATE decreases over the next week
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly positive when the labor indicators show the described pattern (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and the S&P 500's 5-day realized returns suggests deflationary pressure that can support positive 60-day forward returns as investors anticipate lower discount rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during a baseline of stable inflation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as signaled by FEDFUNDS rising), S&P 500 forward returns tend to be negative over the next 20 days regardless of other macro variables, due to reduced credit and equity risk premia.
candidate_trigger: any upward movement in FEDFUNDS during a tightening regime
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not consistently negative across multiple tightening episodes (p > 0.05).
